text_blocks.snippet: Opsumit (macitentan) is a prescription medication used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Like all medications, it can cause various side effects ranging from mild to serious.

list.snippet: Stuffy or runny nose, sore throat, or nasal inflammation (nasopharyngitis)
Anemia (low red blood cell count, which can cause pale skin, unusual tiredness, or weakness)
Fluid retention and peripheral edema (swelling in the hands, legs, ankles, or feet)

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity / Birth Defects: Opsumit can cause severe, life-threatening birth defects if taken during pregnancy. It is strictly contraindicated during pregnancy, and individuals able to become pregnant must use reliable birth control and undergo regular pregnancy testing.

Liver Damage / Hepatotoxicity: Can cause elevated liver enzymes or liver injury. Watch for signs of liver problems like yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, upper-right stomach pain, severe fatigue, or unexplained nausea/vomiting.
Significant Fluid Retention / Pulmonary Edema: Rapid weight gain, severe swelling, or new/worsening breathing difficulties should be reported immediately.
Decreased Sperm Count: Opsumit may reduce sperm counts and impact male fertility.

text_blocks.snippet: For detailed prescribing information, you can check the Official Opsumit Safety Information or review the DailyMed Drug Label.
